title: Cut pantheon-base-v0.18.0 covering the thirteen simplification waves and the post-v0.17.8 tenant waves, then build pantheon-ops against it
goal: The 13-wave simplification programme merged between 2026-10-27 and 2026-10-28, but no foundation release has been cut since v0.17.8 (2026-10-27, commit e256d1fb). pantheon-ops therefore cannot build against a release that contains the waves, which is the one unfinished item on the programme manifest. This package prepares and cuts pantheon-base-v0.18.0 on release/0.18: a minor bump because the waves are an architecture optimisation with governance enhancements per docs/VERSION_MANAGEMENT_GUIDE.md section 2.3, and because the release also carries the tenant lifecycle waves W1/W2/W4/W8 merged after v0.17.8. It ships the four consumable assets, verifies them with Foundation Release Verify, then advances the pantheon-ops lock to 0.18.0 and records a real go build plus frontend build against the synced tree. No product source is modified by this package.
findings: The last foundation release, pantheon-base-v0.17.8, sits at e256d1fb; every one of the thirteen simplification waves plus the tenant lifecycle waves W1/W2/W4/W8 merged after it, so no published release contains them.
docs/reviews/CODE_SIMPLIFICATION_PLAN.md section 11.6 and the programme manifest both leave the pantheon-ops build item open for exactly this reason; the item cannot be closed by documentation.

The batch cannot be a patch: VERSION_MANAGEMENT_GUIDE section 2.3 classifies architecture optimisation and governance enhancement as minor, and W4 changes a login/switch gate plus adds tenant.member.user_not_in_tenant, so 0.18.0 on release/0.18 is the honest level.
No migration moves in this release: the chain still ends at 000030_tenant_plan_definitions (schema 30), which keeps the consumer rebuild a tree swap plus go mod download.

This workstation intermittently times out on github.com:443 while api.github.com answers normally, so clone/fetch/push steps need retries and the local release scripts must not be restarted blindly after a network failure.

implementationNotes: Version level is a judgement recorded in the packet: 0.18.0/release/0.18 rather than 0.17.9, because the simplification waves are an architecture optimisation and the batch also contains tenant behaviour changes. The maintainer can re-level it at acceptance.
The three notes files are authored under .harness/evidence/2026-10-29-v0180-simplification-release/notes/ so both the workflow path (notes_dir) and the local scripts consume the same text.

Publish preconditions are enforced by publish-foundation-release.mjs: clean worktree and a successful Release Gate Summary check on the target commit. The release commit therefore has to reach main and pass CI before the tag is created.
The release body must not present the LOC window as the programme's gain; the window includes net-additive tenant work and is a lower bound.
pantheon-ops already carries an uncommitted 0.17.8 sync in its worktree; the 0.18.0 bump builds on that state and the diff is recorded, not silently rewritten.

executionRoles.implementerPosture: Release bookkeeping only: the diff must contain no product source, and every claim about the waves must trace to a wave evidence file or the plan's execution record.
reviewerPosture: Confirm the version level matches section 2.3 and that the reasoning is recorded.
Confirm the release notes do not claim the LOC window as the programme's gain.
Confirm no product source, workflow or gate file appears in the diff.
Confirm the notes files are non-placeholder and name the two tenant behaviour changes.
Confirm the target commit is the merge commit on main and that the tag was cut from it.

runtimeGap: The release itself is runtime evidence: a tag plus four assets consumed by pantheon-ops. Nothing in this package changes runtime behaviour, so no new UI or API evidence is produced beyond the release artefact checks and the consumer build.
